title: The integral compact-support direct image of a constructible complex is constructible
statement: Let $K_0$ be a field, let $X,Y$ be finite-type $K_0$-schemes and $f:X\to Y$ a separated finite-type $K_0$-morphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Fix a prime $\ell$ invertible in $K_0$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Choose a compactification $c=(j,\bar f)$ of $f$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements] and let $Rf_{!,n}=R\bar f_{*,n}j_!:D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,n})\to D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,n})$ be the compact-support candidate attached to $c$ [def-weil-compact-support-candidate]. Let $K\in D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$ be an object of the derived-complete integral category [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], and put $K_n=K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}$, the derived reduction [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction]. The objects $M_n=\operatorname{Res}_nRf_{!,n}K_n$ of $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$, with $\operatorname{Res}_n$ the restriction of scalars of the completed coefficient sheaf [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] applied termwise [lem-weil-restriction-of-scalars-exact], form an inverse system whose transition map $M_{n+1}\to M_n$ is $\operatorname{Res}_{n+1}$ applied to the composite of $Rf_{!,n+1}$ of the reduction map $K_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}^{A_{E,n+1}}_{A_{E,n}}K_n$ with the isomorphism $Rf_{!,n+1}\operatorname{Res}^{A_{E,n+1}}_{A_{E,n}}\cong\operatorname{Res}^{A_{E,n+1}}_{A_{E,n}}Rf_{!,n}$ of [lem-sf-compact-support-restriction-of-scalars]. Then every derived limit $M=R\varprojlim_nM_n$ of this system in $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-limit] lies in $D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$: it is derived complete, and for every $n\geq1$ the reduction $M\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}$ lies in $D^b_c(Y,A_{E,n})$ [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility], with cohomological supports in one interval independent of $n$.

proof.text: Write $A=\mathcal O_E$, $P_n=A_{E,n}$ and $R_T=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,T}$. The compactification is $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{\bar f}Y$, with $\bar f$ proper and therefore of finite type [def-weil-compactifications-refinements, def-weil-proper-morphism]. The composite $\overline X\to Y\to\operatorname{Spec}K_0$ is of finite type: finite affine covers compose, and if a ring is generated by finitely many elements over a finitely generated algebra, the union of the two finite sets generates it over the base. This verifies the finite-type definition [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. A field is Noetherian because its only ideals are zero and itself; hence $X,Y,\overline X$ are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. For an affine open $V\subseteq\overline X$, $j^{-1}V$ is an open subscheme of the Noetherian scheme $X$, so is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. Thus $j$ is quasi-compact. Choose a closed subscheme $i:Z\hookrightarrow\overline X$ with image $\overline X\setminus X$ using [lem-weil-pbc-closed-subset-closed-subscheme]. The coefficient identifications $j^{-1}R_{\overline X}\cong R_X$ and $j^{-1}(P_n)_{\overline X}\cong(P_n)_X$ commute with all quotient projections by [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image]. Consequently the ringed open--closed lemma [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] supplies extension by zero $J=j_!$ for these completed rings, as well as for each finite ring: it is exact, left adjoint to restriction, and satisfies $j^{-1}J=\mathrm{id}$, $i^{-1}J=0$, and $0\to Jj^{-1}F\to F\to i_*i^{-1}F\to0$. In what follows completed coefficients always mean $R_T$, never the discrete constant sheaf $A_T$.

source.place: Tags 09AH (lemma-ses-associated-to-open), 09AG (lemma-jshriek-zero), 09BN (lemma-open-immersion); preliminary Noetherian and coefficient checks

proof.text: For any countable family of $R_X$-module sheaves $F_n$, put $P=\prod_nJF_n$. Both $j^{-1}$ and $i^{-1}$ preserve products by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-immersion-limit-preservation], so $j^{-1}P\cong\prod_nF_n$ and $i^{-1}P\cong\prod_n0=0$. The short exact sequence of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] applied to $P$ therefore identifies its counit $J(\prod_nF_n)\to P$ with an isomorphism. This is the canonical product comparison, since its $n$-th projection is $J$ of the $n$-th projection on the open part. Countable products of module sheaves are exact [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact]; hence their derived products are represented termwise by [lem-weil-derived-limit-existence, clause 2]. Exactness of $J$ makes its termwise functor on derived categories triangulated [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. Applying the preceding sheaf comparison in every degree proves that this derived $J$ preserves countable products and their projections. Additivity then identifies $J(1-s)$ with $1-s$ for the tower obtained by applying $J$ to every transition map. This proves precisely the product assertion needed for the Roos triangle, without assuming that every triangulated functor preserves infinite products.

source.place: Lemma 6.1.13, expanded with the ringed open--closed sequence; Stacks Tags 09AH and 015F

proof.text: Set $L=JK$. We next identify its reductions, including their maps. Identify $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ with $\overline X_{\mathrm{proet}}/X$ using [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization]. On this localized ringed site, [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-extension-tensor] gives $J(G\otimes j^{-1}F)\cong JG\otimes F$, natural in $G,F$. Since $J\dashv j^{-1}$, it preserves small direct sums by [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits]; thus the tensor formula applies to total tensor complexes as well, including the sums along each total degree. Choose a K-flat resolution $Q\to K$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. For an acyclic $R_{\overline X}$-complex $C$, exactness of restriction makes $j^{-1}C$ acyclic [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-immersion-limit-preservation]; K-flatness gives $Q\otimes j^{-1}C$ acyclic [def-pc-kflat-complex]; and exactness of $J$ gives $JQ\otimes C\cong J(Q\otimes j^{-1}C)$ acyclic [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed]. Hence $JQ$ is K-flat and resolves $L$.

source.place: Tag 0E8I (lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor); K-flat specialization to finite coefficient reduction

proof.text: Use the K-flat resolution $JQ\to L$ of step 3. Computing reductions as in [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction] gives isomorphisms of $P_n$-complexes $\alpha_n:L\otimes^L_A P_n\xrightarrow{\sim}j_!(K\otimes^L_A P_n)=j_!K_n$. Here extending $Q\otimes_{R_X}(P_n)_X$ by zero and extending $Q$ before tensoring give the same scalar action, by the natural tensor formula and the coefficient identifications of step 1. The presheaf defining extension by zero is the given sheaf on objects factoring through $X$ and zero otherwise, and module sheafification has underlying abelian sheaf equal to abelian sheafification [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface]. The uniqueness of the sheafified scalar action in that statement shows that forgetting coefficients leaves the same extension-by-zero sheaf. In particular $J\operatorname{Res}_n=\operatorname{Res}_n j_!$. For the quotient $\rho_n:P_{n+1}\to P_n$, naturality gives $\alpha_n\circ(\mathrm{id}_{JQ}\otimes\rho_n)=j_!(\mathrm{id}_Q\otimes\rho_n)\circ\alpha_{n+1}$ after restriction of scalars. For the maps from $L$, the same formula with $q\mapsto q\otimes1$ identifies them with $J$ of the reduction maps from $K$. Thus these are identifications of reduction towers with their maps from the original objects, not just of isolated reductions. The resolution-independence assertion [lem-weil-integral-reduction-tower-well-defined] ensures that these quotient maps and units are exactly the intrinsic reduction-tower maps, for any representatives chosen in the item.

source.place: Tag 0E8I (lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor); K-flat specialization to finite coefficient reduction

proof.text: Since $K$ is derived complete, its reduction maps $c_n:K\to\operatorname{Res}_nK_n$ form the first map of a distinguished Roos triangle [def-weil-derived-complete]. Apply the triangulated functor $J$ [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. By step 2 its two product terms and middle arrow become $\prod_nJ\operatorname{Res}_nK_n$ and the transition endomorphism $1-s$. By step 4 these terms and all their projections are precisely the restricted reductions of $L$, and the first map has components the reduction units $L\to\operatorname{Res}_n(L\otimes_A^LP_n)$. The resulting distinguished triangle is therefore the one required by [def-weil-derived-complete] for $L$. This proves derived completeness of $L$ using the project's Roos-triangle definition, without choosing a functorial homotopy limit.

source.place: Lemma 6.1.13 applied to the completion triangle; Definition 3.5.2 interpreted through the Roos triangle

proof.text: The hypothesis $K\in D^b_c(X,A)$ supplies an interval $[a,b]$ containing the cohomological supports of all $K_n$, and constructibility of each $K_n$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. For fixed $n,r$, exactness of finite-level $j_!$ gives $\mathcal H^r(j_!K_n)=j_!\mathcal H^r(K_n)$ [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed]; this identity follows by applying the exact functor to the kernels and images of the differentials. Take a finite stratification of $X$ on which $\mathcal H^r(K_n)$ is locally constant with finite module stalks [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]. Regard its strata as locally closed subschemes of $\overline X$ and add the closed complement $Z$: locally closed in an open subset is locally closed in the whole space. For any open subsets $O,W$ of $\overline X$, $O\cap W$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. Thus every open is retrocompact. Each locally closed subset is $O\cap(\overline X\setminus V)$ for opens $O,V$, hence is constructible by [def-weil-constructible-subset]. On the old strata the restriction of $j_!\mathcal H^r(K_n)$ is the original restriction because $j^{-1}j_!=\mathrm{id}$; on $Z$ it is zero because $i^{-1}j_!=0$ [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed]. Zero is the constant finite zero module. This is exactly the finite-torsion constructibility definition. Thus every $j_!K_n$ is bounded constructible with cohomology in the same interval $[a,b]$. By step 4 these are the reductions of $L$; together with step 5 this proves $L\in D^b_c(\overline X,A)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed].

source.place: Lemma 6.7.7: extension by zero preserves constructibility; explicit finite-stratification argument

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-integral-direct-image-constructible] to the finite-type $K_0$-morphism $\bar f:\overline X\to Y$ and the integral constructible object $L$. Its hypotheses hold by steps 1 and 6, and $\ell$ is still invertible in $K_0$. It gives a tower-defined object $T=R\bar f_*L$ which is derived complete, whose reductions are $R\bar f_{*,n}L_n$ with $L_n=L\otimes_A^LP_n$, and an integer $N$ independent of $n$ such that these reductions are bounded constructible with supports in $[a,b+N]$. This is an assertion about reductions of the completed coefficient sheaf; it assumes no finite cohomological dimension on arbitrary pro-etale sheaves. The definition [def-weil-derived-direct-image] makes $T$ a derived limit of $N_n=\operatorname{Res}_n R\bar f_{*,n}L_n$ with the quotient-induced transition maps.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.2, applied to the proper factor; Lemma 6.7.7

proof.text: For each $n$, applying $R\bar f_{*,n}$ to $\alpha_n$ of step 4 gives $\beta_n:N_n\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Res}_nR\bar f_{*,n}j_!K_n=M_n$, using the compact-support candidate $Rf_{!,n}=R\bar f_{*,n}j_!$ [def-weil-compact-support-candidate]. This is an isomorphism of inverse systems, not merely termwise: on the chosen resolution the input transition is $\mathrm{id}_Q\otimes\rho_n$, and step 4 identifies its extension by zero with the transition for $L_n$. The restriction-of-scalars comparison in [lem-sf-compact-support-restriction-of-scalars] is explicitly the composite of the extension-by-zero coefficient identification and the direct-image coefficient comparison. To check that square explicitly, write $R_n=R\bar f_{*,n}$, $S_n=\operatorname{Res}^{P_{n+1}}_{P_n}$, and let $d_n:L_{n+1}\to S_nL_n$ and $e_n:K_{n+1}\to S_nK_n$ be the reduction transitions. Step 4 gives $S_n(\alpha_n)\circ d_n=j_!(e_n)\circ\alpha_{n+1}$, using $j_!S_n=S_nj_!$. Let $C_n(U):R_{n+1}S_nU\xrightarrow{\sim}S_nR_nU$ be the natural direct-image comparison [lem-weil-proetale-direct-image-restriction-of-scalars]. Apply $R_{n+1}$ to the preceding equality and then use the naturality identity $S_nR_n(\alpha_n)\circ C_n(L_n)=C_n(j_!K_n)\circ R_{n+1}S_n(\alpha_n)$. The result is $S_nR_n(\alpha_n)\circ C_n(L_n)\circ R_{n+1}(d_n)=C_n(j_!K_n)\circ R_{n+1}(j_!e_n)\circ R_{n+1}(\alpha_{n+1})$. After $\operatorname{Res}_{n+1}$ this reads $\beta_n\circ t^N_n=t^M_n\circ\beta_{n+1}$: the left transition is the one in [def-weil-derived-direct-image], and the right transition is exactly the composite specified in the item because its compact-support comparison is $C_n$ after the extension-by-zero identification.

source.place: Tag 0H9J (remark-functoriality-derived-limit), with the prescribed coefficient comparisons

proof.text: The isomorphism of inverse systems in step 8 compares the tower defining $T$ with the tower in the statement. Let $M$ be any derived limit of this system, as in the question. Apply [lem-weil-derived-limit-morphism] to $(\beta_n)_n$ and the Roos triangles of $T$ and $M$ to obtain a triangle morphism; [lem-weil-derived-limit-levelwise-iso] makes its first component $T\to M$ an isomorphism. Hence the conclusion applies to every possible derived limit, without claiming a canonical isomorphism between arbitrary choices.

source.place: Tag 0H9J (remark-functoriality-derived-limit), with the prescribed coefficient comparisons

proof.text: Let $h:T\xrightarrow{\sim}M$ be the isomorphism from step 9 and $h_n:T\otimes_A^LP_n\xrightarrow{\sim}M\otimes_A^LP_n$ its derived reductions [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction]. The reduction units are the units of the natural adjunction [lem-weil-derived-scalar-extension-restriction-adjunction], so $\operatorname{Res}_n(h_n)c^T_n=c^M_nh$ for every $n$. Their quotient-induced transitions commute with $h_n$: on a K-flat representative of a morphism this is $(u\otimes\mathrm{id}_{P_n})(\mathrm{id}\otimes\rho_n)=(\mathrm{id}\otimes\rho_n)(u\otimes\mathrm{id}_{P_{n+1}})$, and this equality passes to the localization, since naturality for a chain map also gives naturality for the inverse of a quasi-isomorphism and hence for a roof. The resolution comparisons preserve both units and transitions [lem-weil-integral-reduction-tower-well-defined]. Taking products thus identifies the first arrow and $1-s$ of the completeness triangle for $T$ with the required arrows for $M$. The triangle obtained through $(h,\prod_n\operatorname{Res}_n h_n,\prod_n\operatorname{Res}_n h_n)$ is distinguished and proves derived completeness of $M$ [def-weil-derived-complete]. Each reduction of $M$ is isomorphic to the corresponding reduction of $T$. Step 7 therefore gives finite-torsion constructibility of every reduction and the common cohomological interval $[a,b+N]$. These three properties are precisely membership in $D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], and prove all clauses of the item.
